system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Seller Draft Review (Buyer's Side)

Below, each issue sets out the **Seller's position**, **what we should want** (per playbook), and my **recommendation + one-line reason**.

---

**SPA-N-001 — General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- *We want:* Start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 25% / 6,000,000.** The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft — none given, so we cannot accept it.

**SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only excess above basket recoverable.
- *We want:* De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject on all three points.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and convert the basket into a deductible — materially narrows recovery.

**SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; and all Claims subject to limitations unless stated otherwise.
- *We want:* 24 months; 18 months only as a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval (none given).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; insist on 24 months** and delete the "applies to all Claims" sweep-up (see SPA-N-004/-014).

**SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity/title warranties folded into general caps and time limits "for simplicity."
- *We want:* Separate regime — 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject firmly.** Collapsing title/capacity into the general cap is a major erosion of core protection, not an admin convenience.

**SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Silent; limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance stated to apply to "all Claims of any nature" (Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- *We want:* Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent.
- *Recommendation:* **Insert express carve-out; non-negotiable.** The "all Claims" wording would purport to cap fraud — unacceptable and no one may waive this.

**SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General/deemed disclosure of the whole data room, Accounts, statutory and public registers (Sch 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]).
- *We want:* Specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room/public-register/prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject deemed disclosure.** Require each disclosed matter to be specific and fairly disclosed with sufficient detail.

**SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for anything Buyer/advisers knew or that was "discoverable" from data room or public records (Cl. 8.3).
- *We want:* Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **Delete, especially the "discoverable" limb.** Constructive/deemed-knowledge bar combined with deemed disclosure would gut the warranties.

**SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied "on delivery" of counterparty's written consent.
- *We want:* Effective consent AND evidence its conditions (11.3) are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material (~30% revenue) customer.
- *Recommendation:* **Make effective consent + evidenced condition satisfaction a Completion condition.** No consent/evidence is currently in the data room (Disclosure §2); delivery-only is not enough.

**SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3,200,000; release "to be provided following Completion."
- *We want:* Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- *Recommendation:* **Require payoff + direct repayment + security discharge at Completion.** Debt-free/cash-free basis; no discharge is in the data room (Disclosure §3).

**SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow; on-costs silent.
- *We want:* AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super) as a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- *Recommendation:* **Require explicit funding + on-costs.** "Matter for the Seller" without a funds-flow line risks the liability landing on the Company post-Completion.

**SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "adequate."
- *We want:* Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is unverified either way.
- *Recommendation:* **Broaden to cover failed SOW3 Materials transfer/assignment and consequences**, not just the fee. No payment receipt or assignment is in the data room (Disclosure §4).

**SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* DD-006 "preliminary," "not expected to be material"; no confirmed breach/loss.
- *We want:* Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- *Recommendation:* **Add preservation/investigation/update covenants (and consider specific indemnity for the incident).** Don't accept the "not material" characterisation, but don't assert a breach either.

**SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- *We want:* Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- *Recommendation:* **Diligence terminability/avoidability; reserve position.** Disclosure doesn't state whether unavoidable/accrued — don't concede ordinary-course until verified.

**SPA-N-014 — Category separation**
- *Seller:* Limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5; time-limit sweep-up).
- *We want:* Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the sweep-up; add express "subject to the Fundamental/Title and specific-indemnity regimes" wording.** Prevents the general cap silently swallowing protected categories.

**SPA-N-015 — Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
- *We want:* Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- *Recommendation:* **Require independent verification** (ASIC searches, encumbrance/PPSR checks, board/shareholder authority). Seller's own register is not independent proof.

**SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Treats tax and IP as "settled under the general regime."
- *We want:* These remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject "settled"; mark as open.** Folding tax/IP into the general regime is premature and ties to the SPA-N-004/-014 category-separation point.

---

**Cross-cutting flags for the deal team:**
1. Three positions require **Amelia Frost's written authority that has not been given** — 20% cap (001), 18-month period (003), and any post-completion Riverlark release (009). We cannot concede these at our level.
2. The **"all Claims" sweep-up language (003/004/005/014)** is the single most damaging drafting move — it simultaneously caps fundamentals, caps fraud, and overrides category separation. Treat as a package.
3. **Deemed disclosure (006) + constructive-knowledge bar (007)** combine to hollow out the warranties; resist them together.

Want me to draft the mark-up / issues list or a response letter to Seller's counsel next?
=== END ADVICE ===
